$comment: ADAAAA-7767 - american-football audio-trigger eval corpus. One measured class: the crowd/PA roar around a scoring play. Onsets are the frame-verified score-bug transitions in evals/american_football_val/label-manifest.json (first 1 fps frame whose digits show the new score). Negatives are score-stable 24 s windows from the same clip: no scoring transition inside the window by the score bug at both ends. The clip is a box-side clip-root artifact (CC0 1.0, sha256 in the label manifest); it is not committed to the repo. The match window is widened to -6 s/+3 s because the community-access operator updates the score bug a few seconds after the play, so an onset is bounded by the recording, not by the snap.

classes.gap_reason: Football has a real whistle/PA cue, but in football the whistle marks EVERY play ending (a dead-ball signal, tens per quarter), not a scoring cue. Labelling it as a scoring-trigger class would measure a signal that fires on every down and would inflate the candidate count without carrying the type. Recorded as an explicit gap, not as a pass; the whistle class in evals/audio-labels.json is untouched and is not re-used as a football result.
